title: Case Series Investigating the Efficacy and Safety of Bilateral Fluocinolone Acetonide (ILUVIEN®) in Patients with Diabetic Macular Edema: 10 Eyes with 12 Months Follow-up

license.statement: CC BY-NC 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International License); non-commercial, so private

condition: Bilateral chronic diabetic macular edema in pseudophakic eyes, previously treated with macular laser and anti-VEGF (most also with intravitreal triamcinolone); case series of 10 eyes of 5 patients, both eyes implanted at different dates, 12-month follow-up

groups.agent: fluocinolone acetonide intravitreal implant 0.2 ug/day (ILUVIEN), one implant per eye
groups.description: All 10 eyes (both eyes of 5 patients; the fellow eye implanted at a later visit, each eye followed from its own implant); marketed implant, no experimental arm

cells.definition: definition:change from baseline is 0 at baseline; Table 2 6- and 12-month cells are mean changes from baseline (Case Series text: 'Table 2 shows the mean changes from baseline')

series.baseline_label: Baseline before the implant (Table 2 row 'Central retinal thickness, um', column 2)
series.notes: Central retinal thickness in um, no subfield definition; mean ± SD (Table 2 footnote); the 6- and 12-month cells are signed mean changes from baseline (the column headers do not say 'change'; the text states that Table 2 shows mean changes); OCT device not named in the article; months after the implant; per-visit n not reported

exclusions.what: Percent change in CRT given in the Case Series text
exclusions.reason: not a table cell; the um change series from the same eyes is used

exclusions.what: Figure 1 per-eye CRT plots and per-patient changes quoted in the text
exclusions.reason: figure values and partial text values are not citable table cells

exclusions.what: Table 2 visual acuity and IOP rows
exclusions.reason: visual acuity and IOP are not extracted

notes: Prior treatment: all eyes had macular laser and intravitreal anti-VEGF before the implant (Table 1 and text)
The article does not name the OCT device or scan; central retinal thickness in um is taken as the reported OCT value (device 'unstated')
Both eyes of each patient are included (n = 10 eyes of 5 patients)
